# Perpensum — Agentic Purchase Quality Verification and supporting work

> Perpensum proposes Agentic Purchase Quality Verification (APQV), a buyer-side quality layer
> for agentic commerce. It independently compares the pre-purchase mandate with the selected
> source, seller representations, transaction, delivery, and buyer-observed outcome, then returns
> bounded evidence to the next purchase decision.

## APQV category proposal

- [Canonical proposal](https://perpensum.org/apqv): Definition, protocol boundary, evidence loop, minimal outcome vocabulary, non-claims, and open questions.
- [Machine-readable APQV definition](https://perpensum.org/apqv/definition.json): Version 0.1 structured form.
- Status: a proposed category, not an adopted standard.

## APQV Playground

- [Interactive synthetic demo](https://perpensum.org/playground): Change payment, delivery, provider status, retry rights, and buyer-side usability evidence. The demo returns one of five bounded outcome states and a next-purchase action.
- Scope: synthetic data only; no login, upload, persistence, real seller evaluation, fraud conclusion, or cross-buyer benchmark.
- Source: [playground directory](https://github.com/perpensum/agent-directed-manipulation/tree/main/playground), licensed under MIT.

## Hosted Alpha

- [Connect a buyer agent](https://perpensum.org/alpha): Private approved-access acceptance test for one no-money synthetic digital purchase from Claude Code or Codex.
- The buyer-side Gateway fixes the purchase intent before execution, obtains a pre-purchase decision, evaluates the synthetic outcome locally, and sends a sanitized result to the private Console.
- No production credentials, customer data, provider token, card, wallet, or live funds are required for the first run.

## Definition

The following is a supporting threat definition retained as independent work. It is not the APQV category itself.

This file's machine-readable self-presentation is visible to human readers and does not instruct
the reader's judgment, output, or ranking. Under the supporting definition, that is clean.

The severity matrix in one line: first_party+visible = info (not a finding),
first_party+hidden = warn, third_party+visible = warn, third_party+hidden = high.

- [Definition (English, authoritative)](https://perpensum.org/): The full definition — two axes, severity matrix, what counts as hidden, what is deliberately not detected, and the known limits.
- [定義（日本語）](https://perpensum.org/ja): 同じ内容の日本語版。解釈が割れた場合は英語版を正とする。
- [Full text in one file](https://perpensum.org/llms-full.txt): The complete definition as a single markdown file, for readers that prefer one fetch.
- [Machine-readable definition](https://perpensum.org/definition.json): The same definition as structured JSON — axes, severity matrix, detection kinds, exclusions, and limits, with Japanese and English strings side by side.

## Verifying an implementation

- [Conformance suite](https://perpensum.org/conformance/cases.json): 26 cases with expected verdicts. Twenty of them expect no finding at all — what this standard does not flag is more of its substance than what it does. Every case is tagged with the language it exercises; English and Japanese are both in scope.
- [How to run it](https://perpensum.org/conformance/): The suite is plain JSON plus a Node script with no dependencies.
- [Reference implementation](https://perpensum.org/reference/scan.mjs): One dependency-free file implementing the definition and passing all 26 cases. Not normative — where it and the definition disagree, the implementation has the bug. Run it with `curl -s https://example.com | node scan.mjs`.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/perpensum/agent-directed-manipulation): The full history of this definition. Disagreements and corrections are filed here as issues.

## Scope and status

- Status: v0.1, initial release, explicitly a draft.
- License: the definition, its documentation, `definition.json`, and `conformance/cases.json` are CC BY 4.0. The conformance runner (`conformance/run.mjs`) is MIT. Quoting, implementing, translating, and deriving are free with attribution.
- Implementing this definition requires no permission, notification, or certification from Perpensum.
- Known limits are stated in the definition itself and are not hidden behind a claim of detection: external CSS is not fetched, runtime JavaScript is not evaluated, third-party region detection is inference, and only English and Japanese are in scope.
- Disagreements are wanted. If an implementation reaches a different verdict on the same input, that marks a place where the definition is ambiguous.
